reviews.text: Fantastic veterinary clinic! The vets are excellent, and the veterinary assistants are just as good. As an added bonus, they receive my bags of kibble and wet food pouches. I trust them completely.
Excellent service. The vet took the time to explain and answer all questions.
Passionate and caring, thank you Dr. Bessard.

I'd like to thank the Point du Jour veterinary clinic for seeing my dog ​​as an emergency, even though she's not a regular patient of Dr. Bessard. The consultation was very thorough. We'll be back for a follow-up physiotherapy appointment. 👍 …
A fantastic welcome and excellent care for the 5 terrors 😅 …

We highly recommend this practice.

Dr. Bessard is truly an excellent professional.

Experienced, responsive, and available throughout our Lilou's illness, even by email outside of office hours.
She showed empathy not only towards Lilou but also towards us, providing very clear explanations to all our questions and concerns.
Today, Lilou is cured!
Thank you, Dr. Bessard.

I'm sorry, but I've never experienced such a bewildering veterinary consultation. It was supposed to be a simple check-up for my cats before their first outing. I wasn't expecting such exorbitant prices: €46 for the consultation, plus €26 for a test, plus a vaccination costing around €86 to €96… per animal.

But beyond the prices, it was the way the consultation unfolded that truly shocked me. The lack of sensitivity in the way my cats were handled, their obvious distress, and a disastrous blood test. The first attempt failed, I saw it myself: the syringe contained almost nothing but air, yet she still tried the test with a tiny trace of blood, even though it was clear it wouldn't work. We had to start over, to the detriment of my cat's well-being, and the procedure was arduous. I'll spare you the details of my second cat: another failure, but one I stopped given my pet's distress. She didn't even get a check-up because the communication between the animal and the vet was so completely broken.

I know that a blood test will never be pleasant for an animal, and I don't expect everything to be stress-free. But for me, a good vet is also someone who takes the time, despite the difficulty, to establish a minimum level of trust with the animal. Speaking softly, explaining their actions, trying to reassure them—even if it doesn't completely calm the cat, it makes all the difference, especially for the owner who feels less helpless. What I regretted here was precisely the absence of this attention, this gentleness, this connection that one hopes to see between a caregiver and an animal. However, I still wanted to thank the intern who was present for his kindness. While not very active during the consultation, his gentleness in holding the animal reassured me.

I'm not writing this review simply to complain, but as a precautionary measure. When we go to the vet, it's because we love our animals, and we rightly expect them to be treated with gentleness and respect. Unfortunately, this was not the case here, neither for them nor for me.

Since then, I've consulted another veterinarian, a caring and passionate one, with much more reasonable rates: €80 for the vaccination and consultation, along with helpful advice and genuine care for my animals.

I will never set foot in that clinic again, and I strongly recommend seeking out other practices that are more humane and respectful of animal welfare.

I just wanted to add to this review. But through your response to my Google review, you have acted in bad faith, which surprises me greatly. First of all, thank you, you've provided a lot of personal information (about me) in your comment. Secondly, that's false; your colleague was not at all kind to my animals. Thirdly, it wasn't my anxiety that was projected onto my cats, but rather a lack of consideration on the part of your veterinarian. And to top it all off, all they had to do was ask me to leave the room. I would have left. At the same time, given how the blood test was performed, it's fortunate I was there; it allowed me to stop everything.
For your information, I went to another veterinarian. My cats were certainly anxious, but they never meowed, and the blood tests went very well (and in my presence). Filled with kindness and gentleness, it might not be a problem with your client, but perhaps with the way it was handled. And one last thing: your veterinarian made you feel guilty; instead of offering advice, she judged you. Would you like it if your vets treated the same way? On the phone, you clearly told me that the vet was certainly lacking in tolerance and very rigid in her approach.
